reviews.text: I had such a happy experience right in the middle of Ebisu.
It has a nice, somewhat Showa-era atmosphere. The dog kept at the shop is friendly and very well-behaved.

I actually visited this pet shop, and seeing the dogs and cats inside made me very sad and worried.

Some of the animal enclosures were rusty and didn't appear to be properly maintained. On several visits, some animals' enclosures lacked water. There were also areas with old, tattered beds and hardly any toys.

Some dogs looked very thin, and overall, many animals seemed lonely and lacked sufficient stimulation.

It was quite different from any pet shop I'd seen before; honestly, it felt more like an animal shelter.

What particularly stuck with me was one Chihuahua for sale.

That puppy looked so lonely, and I repeatedly thought, "I want to take this puppy home and help it." The price wasn't the reason I didn't buy it.

I hesitated because I worried that buying an animal from such conditions would inadvertently support the current situation.

Since I live near this shop, I went back several times to check on that Chihuahua. No matter how many times I went to check, there were no toys in that puppy's space.

So a few days ago, I bought a new toy and left it there for the puppy. I wanted to give it something to play with or distract it, even just a little.

I still think about that Chihuahua.

I sincerely hope that it finds a loving family as soon as possible and can live a safe and happy life.

This review is not intended to attack the store or its staff.

I am writing this because I want to emphasize the importance of providing a safe and secure environment for animals even before they are sold.

For dogs and cats, having access to water, a clean and safe environment, a good bed, enough space, and toys to play with are fundamental aspects of their living environment.

Of course, I understand that pet shops have various costs, such as vaccinations, microchips, food, and medical expenses.

Even so, because it's a place where animals spend long hours every day, I felt that they should value that environment more.

The dogs and cats here are not just "products," but each and every one of them is a precious life.

I sincerely hope that the environment for these animals will improve, even just a little, from now on.

And I hope that all the dogs and cats here will find loving families.

I especially hope that that Chihuahua finds a happy family as soon as possible.

I still can't forget that little one.

I was shocked when I actually saw the inside of the pet shop, which had many dogs and cats.

The animals' living spaces were rusty and dirty, and didn't appear to be kept clean. Often there was no water, the beds were old and torn, and there were hardly any toys. Some looked emaciated, and the dogs and cats seemed very lonely and unhappy, rather than happy.

Honestly, it felt more like an animal shelter or rescue facility than a pet shop.

Seeing the animals was truly heartbreaking; it made me want to cry.

And yet, the prices weren't cheap at all. The animals were being sold at the same price as in a typical, clean, well-equipped pet shop.

I wondered, "Where is all that money going with these high prices?" I understand that there are costs involved in microchipping and vaccinations. However, I think they should prioritize creating a better environment for the animals to live in every day.

Looking at the dogs being sold here, I can't help but wonder, "How long have these puppies been living in these conditions?" If they've been in this state for months, it's truly heartbreaking and cruel.

I don't believe that improvement is impossible due to a lack of money. For example, you can buy pet toys for around 110 yen at Daiso. A new bed can be purchased for around 300-500 yen.

This isn't about money. What I'm trying to say is about the quality of life for these animals.

For example, if a dog is being sold for 220,000 yen, is it really that difficult to provide it with a new bed for around 500 yen or a toy for 110 yen?

I seriously considered taking home one of the Chihuahuas in this store many times. It looked so pitiful, and I felt a strong desire to rescue it. I still think about that dog.

Ultimately, I decided against buying it. It wasn't a matter of price. I still feel the desire to help that dog.

However, knowing that the animals were living in such conditions, I felt that paying money here would inadvertently support the store's practices.

I own other pets, but I've never adopted one from a store with such conditions. When I actually saw it, it felt more like an animal shelter or rescue facility than a pet shop.

Even so, I'm still worried about that Chihuahua.

I live near this store, so I still go to check on her occasionally.

I've visited several times, but she never had any toys.

So the other day, I bought a new toy and brought it to her. I left it there, hoping that she could play a little and feel less lonely.

I sincerely hope that she finds a loving family as soon as possible. And that she will be loved and live a safe and happy life from now on.

I still think about her.

Animals are precious lives before they are merchandise.

Please provide them with the bare necessities: water, a clean environment, a clean bed, enough space, and toys to play with.

It is truly horrible to make animals live in rusty places, dirty environments, torn beds, and empty spaces.

If you cannot properly manage the animals and provide a safe and secure environment, I sincerely hope you will seriously consider whether you should continue operating in this manner.

If this is the first place these animals will live, it is truly heartbreaking that they are starting in such an environment.

The dogs and cats here were not born to live in such conditions.

Please, seriously improve this place. Treat the animals with more care.

I sincerely hope that these animals can live even a little bit happier and more safely.

And I hope that all the dogs and cats here will one day find a family that truly loves them.

It truly breaks my heart.
Animal cruelty. The meerkats had no water and were very stressed. The sheep was in a small cage with no friends despite being a herd animal.

I went to buy crickets.

I think a male and female pair cost a little under 500 yen.

I bought three males and one female.

They accept Suica, Edy, PayPay, etc.

They also sold live stag beetles and rhinoceros beetles, as well as breeding supplies like substrate.

The crickets are already chirping away. Their chirping is lovely and quite charming.
Wild animals should not be kept in small cages, and the capybara desperately needs water. It's a disgrace that this is allowed in Japan. It's cruel and a crime against nature!

I happened to pass by and decided to stop in! 😳✨

I wasn't sure if I was allowed to take pictures inside, so I snapped a photo before going in!

There were dogs, cats, turtles, owls, parakeets, tropical fish, and more inside! 😳✨✨

Next time, I'll ask a staff member if it's okay to take pictures of the animals I'm interested in. 😸

It was just a quick visit, but I was soothed by the animals and had a great time! 😊✨✨(ღ✪ｖ✪)

I'm currently not in a position to keep a pet, so I'm sorry about that. 🙇

The cat I adopted from here passed away after just over three years.
The vet diagnosed it with a congenital condition.
I reported it, stating that it was genetic and therefore problematic, and asked them to inform the breeder, stating the name of the condition, but they just repeated the same old, manual-like response and didn't take me seriously.
I don't know why you think my complaint is a friendly suggestion (or a complaint that should be thrown in the trash), but it seems like they're not listening to what I'm saying, so I decided to write it here.

When I adopted this cat, I also felt very uncomfortable with the way the staff treated me, but it seems like this pet shop has no intention of doing business with a breeder who can guarantee health or taking responsibility for its life at all costs. It seems they just want to stock good-looking animals and sell them because they're just a product.
I don't think this store stocks only unhealthy animals 100% of the time, but if you want to adopt a pet, I wholeheartedly recommend getting one from a reputable breeder. At the very least, you shouldn't adopt one from here.

The middle-aged manager? was very considerate and made the experience pleasant. I hope the sheep that has been unsold for a long time sells soon.

I do not recommend this place.
First, there were two large dogs that weren't on leashes. They might be good dogs, but considering the store has no doors and faces the street, I think they should be kept on leashes just in case.
Also, a baby budgie was in the same cage as a conure and was being bullied. I don't recommend putting birds of such different sizes in a small cage. I felt sorry for the budgie.

It was also strange that the elderly man who seemed to be the manager kept staring at me. He was sneaking around peeking from behind the shelves, which made me uncomfortable. Did he think I was going to shoplift? There were several other animals whose living conditions didn't seem good, and it broke my heart. I will never go there again.
